compoundNote: The site's 'Dynamine (Methylliberine)' page describes ONE compound but its mechanism/benefits text draws on the broader 'purine alkaloid' literature that includes theacrine (Teacrine, a DIFFERENT, structurally related but distinct compound also sold by the same manufacturer, Compound Solutions). This file evaluates both the methylliberine-specific evidence and the adjacent theacrine evidence, and flags where the site's claims implicitly borrow from theacrine or combination-product studies rather than methylliberine alone.

ourClaims.studySummary: Site cites 'A 2020 pharmacokinetic study' and 'A 2019 pilot study' showing improved subjective energy/focus/motivation without heart rate/BP change; site states 'Evidence base is very early — primarily pharmacokinetic and pilot data from Compound Solutions (the manufacturer). No large-scale RCTs published yet.'

humanEffects.notes: Site claims pilot study showed improved energy/alertness ratings at 100mg.
Site claims self-reported improvements; no objective cognitive testing published yet.
Site claims no significant HR/BP change at 100-200mg.

studies.title: Methylliberine Ingestion Improves Various Indices of Affect but Not Cognitive Function in Healthy Men and Women
studies.design: double-blind, randomized, within-subject crossover RCT (La Monica et al.) — the site's own studySummary appears to reference this as the '2019 pilot study'; it is actually 2023 and is the PRIMARY, and only identified, human RCT testing methylliberine ALONE on cognition/mood
studies.population: healthy men and women, mean age 33.5±10.7yr
studies.dose: 100mg methylliberine for 3 days, then tested hourly for 3h on the 4th day, vs placebo
studies.outcome: Stroop test, Trail Making Test-B (objective cognition), visual analog scales for concentration/motivation/mood/energy (subjective)
studies.result: Methylliberine significantly improved SUBJECTIVE concentration (1h, 3h), motivation (3h), mood (1-3h), energy and sustained energy vs placebo (all p≤0.05). Women showed elevated sustained energy specifically. HOWEVER: 'Methylliberine had a negligible influence on cognitive function and vitals (p>0.050)' on the objective Stroop/TMT-B tests — no adverse events reported.
studies.fundingConflict: CONFIRMED (verified via publisher page, not just abstract): funded in part by Compound Solutions, the manufacturer of Dynamine. Co-author Tim N. Ziegenfuss holds several granted patents on methylliberine — a direct financial conflict of interest, though the funder is stated to have had no role in study design/analysis/publication decision.

studies.title: Safety of Short-Term Supplementation with Methylliberine (Dynamine) Alone and in Combination with TeaCrine in Young Adults
studies.design: randomized controlled trial, 5 parallel groups — this is the site's cited '2020 pharmacokinetic study', though it is actually a 4-week safety/biomarker trial, not a pharmacokinetic study
studies.dose: low-dose DYM 100mg, high-dose DYM 150mg, low-dose DYM+TCR (100+50mg), high-dose DYM+TCR (150+25mg), or placebo, daily for 4 weeks
studies.outcome: cardiovascular function (HR, BP, QTc) and blood biomarkers (lipids, CBC, renal/liver markers)
studies.result: Small statistically significant changes over time were found in some cardiovascular and blood biomarkers, but 'no clinically significant changes occurred' — supports the site's cardiovascular-safety claim at these doses, but this trial did NOT test cognitive or focus outcomes at all.
studies.fundingConflict: CONFIRMED (verified via publisher page): funded by Compound Solutions, Inc., the manufacturer of Dynamine and TeaCrine. Authors state no authors 'have a financial or business interest related to the studied products' — no patent conflict disclosed here (contrast with the La Monica 2023 trial).

studies.title: Effects of caffeine, methylliberine, and theacrine on vigilance, marksmanship, and hemodynamic responses in tactical personnel: a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial
studies.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
studies.design: between-subjects, randomized, placebo-controlled RCT — NOTE: this tests methylliberine only as part of a COMBINATION product (150mg caffeine + 100mg methylliberine + 50mg theacrine), never methylliberine alone, so its results cannot be attributed to methylliberine specifically
studies.dose: placebo, 300mg caffeine alone, OR combination 150mg caffeine+100mg methylliberine+50mg theacrine (CMT)
studies.outcome: reaction time, marksmanship, hemodynamics (SBP/DBP), felt arousal after a sustained vigilance task
studies.result: Both caffeine-alone (300mg) and the CMT combination improved vigilance reaction time vs placebo similarly; CMT (with only 150mg caffeine) matched 300mg caffeine's cognitive benefit while producing a smaller diastolic blood pressure rise than caffeine alone. No group differences in marksmanship/movement performance.
studies.fundingConflict: not verified — full text behind paywall in this pass; abstract does not disclose funding

studies.title: Assessing the impact of high theacrine doses on hemodynamic measures, cognitive performance, and physiological stress
studies.design: randomized, double-blind, crossover RCT — THEACRINE (Teacrine), not methylliberine; included here because the site's page conflates the two purine alkaloids
studies.dose: placebo, 3mg/kg, 6mg/kg, or 9mg/kg theacrine — doses higher than the ~200mg typically studied previously
studies.outcome: heart rate, blood pressure, subjective energy, cognitive performance, salivary cortisol and alpha-amylase
studies.result: Higher theacrine doses INCREASED salivary cortisol at 120 and 180min vs placebo — a stress-hormone increase, not the 'clean' stimulant profile the site implies for the purine-alkaloid class. Energy only improved in the PLACEBO condition (not theacrine). No significant effects on heart rate, blood pressure, or cognitive performance at any theacrine dose.
studies.fundingConflict: not stated in abstract; not independently verified

studies.title: A caffeine and theacrine combination improves cognitive performance in tactical personnel under physically fatiguing conditions
studies.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
studies.design: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT — THEACRINE+caffeine combination, not methylliberine
studies.dose: 300mg caffeine (CAF) vs 150mg caffeine+150mg theacrine (CTC) vs placebo
studies.duration: acute, pre/post a high-intensity fatiguing exercise protocol
studies.outcome: Two-Back accuracy/RT, Dynavision Go/NoGo RT, Object Hit & Avoid accuracy
studies.result: Both CAF and CTC improved cognitive performance vs placebo; CTC (half the caffeine dose, plus theacrine) showed additional benefits beyond CAF alone on some measures (higher Two-Back accuracy, faster/less-variable RT). Suggests theacrine may allow a lower effective caffeine dose, not that theacrine works alone.
studies.fundingConflict: not stated in abstract; not independently verified

studies.title: The effects of TeaCrine and caffeine on endurance and cognitive performance during a simulated match in high-level soccer players
studies.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
studies.design: RCT, 4 randomized sessions crossover — THEACRINE, not methylliberine
studies.population: high-level male and female soccer players, n=24
studies.dose: TeaCrine alone, caffeine alone, TeaCrine+caffeine, or placebo (specific mg not stated in abstract)
studies.duration: acute, during a 90-min simulated soccer match
studies.outcome: simple/choice reaction time, cognitive-load RT, time-to-exhaustion (TTE)
studies.result: TTE trended toward significance for TeaCrine and TeaCrine+caffeine vs placebo (P<0.052, not significant). Choice RT was faster in caffeine and TeaCrine+caffeine vs placebo; TeaCrine ALONE did not significantly improve choice RT vs placebo — combination, not standalone theacrine, drove the cognitive benefit.
studies.fundingConflict: not stated in abstract; not independently verified

verdicts.claim: Subjective Energy — evidenceStrength preliminary, 1 study, 'pilot study showed improved energy and alertness ratings at 100mg'
verdicts.reason: Accurately and honestly labeled 'preliminary' with a correct single-study count; La Monica 2023 (the actual RCT, though the site's date reference of '2019' is off by several years) confirms improved subjective energy and sustained energy vs placebo at 100mg.

verdicts.claim: Focus & Motivation — evidenceStrength preliminary, 'self-reported improvements... no objective cognitive testing published yet'
verdicts.reason: This is technically inaccurate, not just imprecise: objective cognitive testing (Stroop, Trail Making Test-B) WAS published in the same 2023 RCT the site is drawing on, and it found methylliberine had 'negligible influence on cognitive function' — i.e. the one objective test that exists is a NULL result, which the site omits entirely while implying objective testing simply doesn't exist yet.

verdicts.claim: Cardiovascular Safety — evidenceStrength moderate, magnitude negligible, 2 studies, 'no significant change in heart rate or blood pressure at 100-200mg'
verdicts.reason: VanDusseldorp 2020 (n=125, 4 weeks) found no clinically significant cardiovascular changes at 100-150mg methylliberine alone or combined with theacrine; consistent with the site's claim, though this trial did not test cognition at all.

verdicts.claim: General framing: 'Unlike caffeine, early evidence suggests minimal tolerance development' and clean stimulant profile implied for the broader purine-alkaloid class
verdicts.reason: No long-term (multi-week) tolerance study of methylliberine was found — the 4-week VanDusseldorp trial measured safety biomarkers, not tolerance/efficacy decay. Separately, a 2026 theacrine dose-escalation RCT found HIGHER theacrine doses (6-9mg/kg) increased salivary cortisol, a stress-hormone signal the site's 'clean stimulant' framing for the alkaloid class does not acknowledge.

doseAssessment.trialRange: Methylliberine alone: 100mg (La Monica 2023) and 100-150mg (VanDusseldorp 2020 safety trial) — the site's 100-200mg range is at or slightly above the highest dose with any published human data (150mg); no human trial has tested 200mg methylliberine alone.
doseAssessment.suggestedText: Narrow the top of the stated range to 150mg, the highest dose actually tested in a published human trial (VanDusseldorp 2020); flag that no published human RCT has tested methylliberine at 200mg.

safetySignals.signal: The ONLY human RCT testing methylliberine's cognitive effects (La Monica 2023, n=25) found it had 'negligible influence on cognitive function' on objective testing — despite subjective concentration/mood/motivation improvements. The site's benefits list ('Improved focus and motivation') does not disclose this objective null result.

Both identified methylliberine-specific human trials (La Monica 2023, VanDusseldorp 2020) were funded in whole or part by Compound Solutions, Inc., the company that trademarks and sells Dynamine and TeaCrine; one trial's co-author (Ziegenfuss) holds patents on methylliberine itself. This is a direct, confirmed manufacturer-funding and patent-holder conflict pattern across the entire methylliberine human evidence base.

Total count of human RCTs on methylliberine specifically found in this search: THREE — one testing cognition/mood alone (La Monica 2023, n=25), one testing 4-week cardiovascular/blood safety alone or with theacrine (VanDusseldorp 2020, n=125), and one testing it only as part of a 3-ingredient combination product confounded with caffeine and theacrine (Cintineo 2022, n=48). No published RCT isolates methylliberine's cognitive effects against an active caffeine comparator, and no RCT has tested chronic (multi-week) cognitive effects.

gaps: The site's studySummary dates ('A 2020 pharmacokinetic study', 'A 2019 pilot study') do not match the actual publication years or study types of the identified trials (VanDusseldorp 2020 is a 4-week safety trial, not pharmacokinetic; La Monica, the closest match to the 'pilot study' claim, is dated 2023, not 2019) — dates and study-type descriptions should be corrected or sourced to a different, unidentified pair of studies.
Site's benefits/humanEffects sections omit the La Monica 2023 objective-cognition null result entirely, creating a materially rosier picture than the primary trial supports.
No evidence was found — supportive or contradictory — for the site's specific claim that Dynamine shows 'minimal tolerance development'; this appears to be an extrapolation, not a trial finding.

The site's mechanism/benefits text draws implicitly on theacrine (TeaCrine) and combination-product literature, which is more extensive than the methylliberine-only evidence base but describes a materially different molecule; a 2026 theacrine dose-response RCT found no cognitive benefit and an unexpected cortisol increase at higher doses, complicating the site's 'clean stimulant' framing for the alkaloid class as a whole.

Pregnancy caution ('Not recommended during pregnancy') has no cited or identifiable supporting trial — reasonable as a precaution given the sparse safety data overall, but should be labeled as precautionary rather than evidence-based.
